x: Commentary on Sūrat “al-Mumtaḥana.” In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.
Discussion of the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted:
h

O you who have believed, do not take My enemy and your enemy as allies, extending to them affection, while they have disbelieved in what came to you of the truth, expelling the Messenger and yourselves because you believe in God, your Lord, if you have come out in jihad in My cause and seeking My approval. You confide to them affection, while I am most knowing of what you concealed and what you declared. And whoever does it among you has certainly strayed from the soundness of the path (1)

He, exalted be His mention, says to those who believe in Him from among the Companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: O you who have believed, do not take My enemy from among the polytheists and your enemy
h
as allies (awliyāʾ)
. He means: as supporters.
And His saying:
h
extending to them affection
. He—majestic be His praise—says: you extend to them your affection for them. The inclusion of the bāʾ in His saying
h
bi-l-mawadda
and its omission are the same, [and it is]
n
comparable to someone’s saying: “urīdu bi-an tadhhaba” and “urīdu an tadhhaba”—the same—and like His saying:
h
and whoever intends therein deviation by wrongdoing
[al-Ḥajj: 25]. The meaning: and whoever intends therein deviation with wrongdoing. And from that is the saying of the poet
n
: “When she hoped for water, there shook the stick
n
at her … a miser who has at the water-trough a groan,” meaning: “when she hoped for the water.”
h
and they have disbelieved in what came to you of the truth

. He says: These polytheists whom I forbade you to take as allies have disbelieved in the truth that came to you from God. That is their disbelief in God and His Messenger, and His Book which He sent down upon His Messenger.
And His saying:
h
expelling the Messenger and yourselves because you believe in God, your Lord

. He—majestic be His praise—says: They expel the Messenger of God and yourselves; meaning: and they expel you as well from your homes and your land. That is the expulsion by the polytheists of Quraysh of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his Companions from Mecca.
And His saying:
h
because you believe in God, your Lord
. He—majestic be His praise—says: They expel the Messenger and yourselves from your homes because you believed in God.
And His saying:
h
if you have come out in jihad in My cause and seeking My approval

is among the postponed [clauses] whose meaning is advancement; the arrangement of the speech is: O you who have believed, do not take My enemy and your enemy as allies, extending to them affection, while they have disbelieved in what came to you of the truth, if you have come out in jihad in My cause and seeking My approval; they expel the Messenger and yourselves because you believe in God, your Lord. And by His saying, exalted be His mention,
h
if you have come out in jihad in My cause

He means: if you have gone out from your homes and emigrated from them to your place of emigration for jihad in My path which I have legislated for you, and My religion which I commanded you, and seeking My approval.
And His saying:
h
You confide to them affection
. He, exalted be His mention, says to the believers from among the Companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: You confide, O believers, affection to the polytheists,
h
while I am most knowing of what you concealed
. He says: And I know better than you what some of you concealed from others and kept secret from him,
h
and what you declared
. He says: and I also know better than you what some of you declared to others,
h
and whoever does it among you has certainly strayed from the soundness of the path
. He—majestic be His praise—says: And whoever of you, O believers, confides affection to the polytheists
h
has certainly strayed

. He says: has deviated from the straight course of the path that God made a way to Paradise and a highway to it. And it is mentioned that these verses from the beginning of this sūra were revealed concerning Ḥāṭib b. Abī Baltaʿa, who had written to Quraysh in Mecca informing them of a matter that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had concealed from them; and the reports and narration came to that effect from a group of the Companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and others.
Mention of those who said that:

c: ʿUbayd b. Ismāʿīl al-Habbārī and al-Faḍl b. al-Ṣabbāḥ told me, they said: Sufyān b. ʿUyayna told us, from ʿAmr b.
m: Dīnār, from Ḥasan b. Muḥammad b. ʿAlī, ʿUbayd Allāh b. Abī Rāfiʿ told me, he said: I heard ʿAlī, may God be pleased with him, say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent me, and al-Zubayr b. al-ʿAwwām, and al-Miqdād—al-Faḍl said: Sufyān said: a group of the Emigrants—and said: “Go until you reach Rawḍat Khākh, for there is a woman traveling in a howdah (ẓaʿīna) with a letter; take it from her.” So we set off, our horses racing us along, until we reached the meadow, and we found a woman, and we said: Bring out the letter. She said: I have no letter. We said: You will bring out the letter, or we will strip off the clothes. So she brought it out from her braids, and we took the letter and went with it to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and in it was: From Ḥāṭib b. Abī Baltaʿa to people in Mecca, informing them of some of the affair of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “O Ḥāṭib, what is this?” He said: O Messenger of God, do not be hasty with me; I was a man attached [to Quraysh] (mulṣaq), having no kinship among them, while those with you of the Emigrants have kin who protect their families in Mecca; so, since that of lineage escaped me, I wished to obtain among them a favor by which they would protect my relatives; and I did not do that out of disbelief or apostasy from my religion, nor out of satisfaction with disbelief after Islam. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “He has told you the truth.” ʿUmar said: O Messenger of God, let me strike the neck of this hypocrite. He said: “He witnessed Badr, and what will let you know—perhaps God has looked upon the people of Badr and said: Do as you wish, for I have forgiven you.” Al-Faḍl added in his narration: Sufyān said: And there was revealed concerning him:
O you who have believed, do not take My enemy and your enemy as allies
until you believe in God alone

c: Ibn Ḥumayd told us, he said: Mihrān told us, from Abū Sinān Saʿīd b.
m: Sinān, from ʿAmr b. Murra al-Jamalī, from Abū al-Bakhtarī al-Ṭāʾī, from al-Ḥārith, from ʿAlī, may God be pleased with him, he said: When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, wished to come to Mecca, he confided to some of his Companions that he intended Mecca—among them Ḥāṭib b. Abī Baltaʿa—and spread among the people that he intended Khaybar; so Ḥāṭib b. Abī Baltaʿa wrote to the people of Mecca that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was coming for you. He said: Then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent me and Abū Marthad, and there was none of us but had a horse, and he said: “Go to Rawḍat Khākh, for you will meet there a woman with a letter; take it from her.” So we set off until we saw her at the place the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had mentioned, and we said: Give the letter. She said: I have no letter. So we put down her baggage and searched, and did not find it in her baggage. Abū Marthad said: Perhaps she does not have it. I said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, neither lied nor was lied to. So we said to her

: Bring out the letter, or we will strip you bare. ʿAmr b. Murra said: So she brought it out from her waistband (ḥujza). And Ḥabīb said: She brought it out from her private part. We brought it to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and behold the letter was from Ḥāṭib b. Abī Baltaʿa to the people of Mecca. ʿUmar stood and said: He has betrayed God and His Messenger; permit me to strike his neck. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Has he not witnessed Badr?” He said: Yes, but he has broken faith and aided Your enemies against You. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Perhaps God has

looked upon the people of Badr and said: Do as you wish.” And ʿUmar’s eyes overflowed, and he said: God and His Messenger know best. Then he sent for Ḥāṭib, and said: “What made you do what you did?” He said: O Prophet of God, I was a man attached to Quraysh, and I had family and wealth there, and there was none of your Companions but had in Mecca someone to protect his family and wealth, so I wrote to them; so that, by God, O Prophet of God, is it—I am indeed a believer in God and in His Messenger. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Ḥāṭib has told the truth, so say nothing to Ḥāṭib but good.” Ḥabīb b. Abī Thābit said: Then God, Mighty and Majestic, revealed:
O you who have believed, do not take My enemy and your enemy

c: Muḥammad b. Saʿd told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told us, he said: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās
m: O you who have believed, do not take My enemy and your enemy as allies, extending to them affection

to the end of the verse: It was revealed concerning a man of Quraysh who was with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Medina; he wrote to his family and clan in Mecca, informing them and warning them that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was marching upon them; the Messenger of God was informed of his letter, so he sent ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭālib, may God be pleased with him, for it, and he brought it to him

c: Ibn Ḥumayd told us, he said: Salama told us, he said: Muḥammad b. Isḥāq told me, from Muḥammad b.
m: Jaʿfar b. al-Zubayr, from ʿUrwa b. al-Zubayr and others of our scholars, they said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, resolved to march to Mecca, Ḥāṭib b. Abī Baltaʿa wrote a letter to Quraysh informing them of what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had resolved of the matter of marching upon them; then he gave it to a woman—Muḥammad b. Jaʿfar claims that she was from Muzayna, and others claimed she was Sāra, a freedwoman of some of the Banū ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib—and he made for her a payment on condition that she deliver it to Quraysh; so she put it in her hair, then twisted her braids over it, then set out with it; and news came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from heaven of what Ḥāṭib had done, so he sent ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭālib and al-Zubayr b. al-ʿAwwām, may God be pleased with them both, and said: “Overtake a woman with whom Ḥāṭib has sent a letter to Quraysh, warning them of what we have gathered for in their affair.” So they set out until they overtook her at al-Ḥulayfa

—the Ḥulayfa of Ibn Abī Aḥmad—and made her dismount, and searched her saddle, and found nothing; and ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭālib, may God be pleased with him, said to her: I swear by God, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not lie, nor did we, and you will bring out this letter to me, or we will uncover you. When she saw his earnestness she said: Turn away from me. He turned away from her, and she undid the braids of her head and drew out the letter and handed it to him, and he came with it to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace; and the Messenger of God summoned Ḥāṭib and said: “O Ḥāṭib, what made you do this?” He said: O Messenger of God, by God, I am indeed a believer in God and His Messenger; I have not changed nor altered, but I was a man who had among the people no root nor clan, and I had in their midst family and a child, so I placated them. ʿAlayhim

. ʿUmar b. al-Khaṭṭāb, may God be pleased with him, said: Let me, O Messenger of God, strike his neck, for the man has become a hypocrite. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “And what will let you know, O ʿUmar, perhaps God has looked upon
the people of Badr on the day of Badr and said: Do as you wish, for I have forgiven you.” So God, Mighty and Majestic, revealed concerning Ḥāṭib:
O you who have believed, do not take My enemy and your enemy as allies
and to You we have turned
[al-Mumtaḥana: 1–4] to the end of the story

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUrwa, he said:
m: O you who have believed, do not take My enemy and your enemy as allies

was revealed concerning Ḥāṭib b. Abī Baltaʿa, who had written a letter to the disbelievers of Quraysh giving them counsel in it, God informed His Prophet, upon him be blessings and peace, of that, so he sent ʿAlī and al-Zubayr and said: “Go, for you will find a woman at such-and-such place; bring the letter that is with her.” They set off until they overtook her, and said: The letter that you have. She said: I have no letter. They said: By God, we will not leave on you

anything without searching it, or you will bring it out. She said: Are you not two Muslims? They said: Yes, but the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, informed us that you have a letter, and our souls are certain that it is with you. When she saw their earnestness she brought out a letter from between her braids, and they went with it to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and in it was: From Ḥāṭib b. Abī Baltaʿa to the disbelievers of Quraysh. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, summoned him and said: “Did you write this letter?” He said: Yes. He said: “What made you do that?” He said: By God, I have not doubted God since I became Muslim, but I was a stranger among you, O clan of Quraysh, and I had in Mecca wealth and sons, so I wished to ward off harm from them by that. ʿUmar, may God be pleased with him, said: Permit me, O Messenger of God, to strike his neck. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Gently, O son of al-Khaṭṭāb! And what will let you know—perhaps God has looked upon the people of Badr and said: Do as you wish, for I am forgiving of you.” Al-Zuhrī said: It was revealed concerning him, down to

: concerning the correspondence of Ḥāṭib b. Abī Baltaʿa and those with him with the disbelievers of Quraysh, warning them

, may God bless him and grant him peace, toward them in the time of al-Ḥudaybiya, and God, Mighty and Majestic, informed His Prophet, upon him be blessings and peace, of that. And it was mentioned to us that they found the letter with a woman in a braid of her hair; so the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, summoned him and said: “What made you do what you did?” He said: By God, I have not doubted the command of God, nor apostatized from it, but I have there

family and wealth, so I wished to placate Quraysh regarding my family and wealth. And it was mentioned to us that he was an ally of Quraysh, not one of themselves; so God, Mighty and Majestic, revealed the Qurʾān concerning that, saying:
If they gain dominance over you, they will be to you enemies and extend toward you their hands and their tongues with evil, and they wish that you would disbelieve

x: Discussion of the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted:
h

If they gain dominance over you, they will be to you enemies and extend toward you their hands and their tongues with evil, and they wish that you would disbelieve (2) Neither your relatives nor your children will benefit you on the Day of Resurrection; He will judge between you; and God, of what you do, is All-Seeing (3)

He, exalted be His mention, says: If these to whom you confide, O believers, affection overpower you, they will be to you at war and enemies, and will stretch toward you their hands with fighting and their tongues with evil.
And His saying:
h
and they wish that you would disbelieve
. He says: and they wish for you that you disbelieve in your Lord, so that you would be like those they are upon.
And His saying:
h
Neither your relatives nor your children will benefit you on the Day of Resurrection

. He, exalted be His mention, says: Let not your relatives, your kin and your children call you to disbelief in God and to taking His enemies as allies, extending to them affection; for neither your relatives nor your children will benefit you with God on the Day of Resurrection, so as to ward off from you God’s punishment on that day, if you disobeyed Him in the world and disbelieved in Him.
And His saying:
h
He will judge between you

. He—majestic be His praise—says: Your Lord will judge between you, O believers, on the Day of Resurrection, by admitting the people of obedience to Him into Paradise, and the people of disobedience to Him and disbelief in Him into the Fire. The reciters differed in the reading of that; most of the reciters of Medina, Mecca and Basra read it (yufṣalu baynakum) with ḍamma on the yāʾ, without shadda on the ṣād and with fatḥa, in the passive
n
. And most of the reciters of Kufa, except ʿĀṣim, read it with ḍamma on the yāʾ and shadda on the ṣād and kasra
n
, meaning: God will distinguish between you, O people. And ʿĀṣim read it with fatḥa on the yāʾ, without shadda on the ṣād, and with kasra
n
, meaning: God will decide between you. And some of the reciters of Syria read (yufaṣṣalu) with ḍamma on the yāʾ and fatḥa and shadda on the ṣād, in the passive
n
. These readings are close in meanings, sound in grammatical analysis; so whichever of them the reader reads, he is correct.

x: And His saying:
h
and God, of what you do, is All-Seeing

. He—majestic be His praise—says: And God, of your deeds, O people, is possessed of knowledge and sight; nothing of them is hidden from Him; He encompasses them all, and He will requite you for them: if good, then good, and if evil, then evil; so fear God regarding yourselves and beware of Him.
Discussion of the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted:
h

There has already been for you an excellent example in Ibrāhīm and those with him, when they said to their people: Indeed, we are disassociated from you and from whatever you worship other than God. We have denied you, and there has appeared between us and you animosity and hatred forever until you believe in God alone—except for the saying of Ibrāhīm to his father: I will surely ask forgiveness for you, though I have not for you anything from God. Our Lord, upon You we have relied, and to You we have turned, and to You is the destination (4)
He, exalted be His mention, says to the believers in Him from among the Companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: There has been for you, O believers,
h
an excellent example
. He says: a good model,
h
in Ibrāhīm
, the Friend of the Most Merciful, whom you emulate,
h
and those with him
from among the prophets of God.

c: As Yūnus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding the saying of God, Mighty and Majestic:
There has already been for you an excellent example in Ibrāhīm and those with him
. He said: Those with him are the prophets

x: And His saying:
h
when they said to their people: Indeed, we are disassociated from you and from whatever you worship other than God
. He says: when they said to their people who disbelieved in God and worshipped the Ṭāghūt: O people, we are disassociated from you and from those whom you worship other than God of gods and rivals.
And His saying:
h
We have denied you, and there has appeared between us and you animosity and hatred forever until you believe in God alone

. He—majestic be His praise—says, relaying the saying of His prophets to their disbelieving people: We have denied you; we rejected the disbelief in God that you were upon, and we repudiated your worship of what you worship other than God as being true, and there has appeared between us and you animosity and hatred forever on account of your disbelief in God, and your worship of what is other than Him, and there is no reconciliation between us and no affection
n
h
until you believe in God alone
. He says: until
n
you affirm God alone, so that you declare Him one and single Him out for worship.
And His saying:
h
except for the saying of Ibrāhīm to his father: I will surely ask forgiveness for you, though I have not for you anything from God

. He, exalted be His mention, says: There has been for you an excellent example in Ibrāhīm and those with him in these matters we have mentioned—separation from the disbelievers, enmity toward them, and abandoning alliance with them—except in the saying of Ibrāhīm to his father:
h
I will surely ask forgiveness for you

. For you have no example in him in that; because that was from Ibrāhīm to his father by reason of a promise he had promised him, before it became clear to him that he was an enemy of God; then, when it became clear to him that he was an enemy of God, he disassociated himself from him. He, exalted be His mention, says: So likewise you, O believers in God: disassociate yourselves from the enemies of God among those who associate others with Him, and do not take them as allies until they believe in God alone and disassociate themselves from the worship of what is other than Him, and show them enmity and hatred.
And in the like of what we have said about that the people of interpretation have spoken.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Muḥammad b. ʿAmr told us, he said: Abū ʿĀṣim told us, he said: ʿĪsā told us, and al-Ḥārith told me, he said: al-Ḥasan told us, he said: Warqāʾ told us,
m: both from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid:
except for the saying of Ibrāhīm to his father
. He said: They were forbidden to take as an example Ibrāhīm’s asking forgiveness for his father, so as to ask forgiveness for the polytheists

c: Ibn Ḥumayd told us, he said: Mihrān told us, from Sufyān, from Abū Jaʿfar, from Muṭarrif al-Ḥārithī, from Mujāhid:
m: I will surely ask forgiveness for you
. He says: in all his affair

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazīd told us, he said: Saʿīd told us, from Qatāda
m: There has already been for you an excellent example in Ibrāhīm
the verse. He says: Take him as an example in everything, except his saying to his father:
I will surely ask forgiveness for you
. Do not take him as an example in that, for it was by reason of a promise he had made him.

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda
m: except for the saying of Ibrāhīm to his father
. He says: Do not take that as an example, for it was a promise upon him, and take as an example all of his affair

c: Yūnus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding the saying of God, Mighty and Majestic:
There has already been for you an excellent example
except for the saying of Ibrāhīm to his father: I will surely ask forgiveness for you
. He said: He says: You have no example in this. And by His saying
though I have not for you anything from God
He means: I cannot ward off from you any punishment from God if God punishes you for your disbelief in Him, nor can I avail you anything against Him.

x: And His saying:
h
Our Lord, upon You we have relied
. He—majestic be His praise—says, relaying the saying of Ibrāhīm and his prophets, God’s blessings upon them:
h
Our Lord, upon You we have relied, and to You we have turned
. He means: and to You we have returned in repentance from what You dislike to what You love and are pleased with;
h
and to You is the destination
. He says: and to You is our destination and our return on the day You raise us from our graves and gather us on the Day of Resurrection to the place of presentation.
Discussion of the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted:
h

Our Lord, make us not a trial for those who disbelieve, and forgive us, our Lord Indeed, it is You who is the Almighty, the Wise (5) There has certainly been for you in them an excellent example for whoever hopes in God and the Last Day. And whoever turns away—then indeed, God is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy (6)

He, exalted be His mention, says, relaying the saying of Ibrāhīm His Friend and those with him: Our Lord, do not make us a trial for those who disbelieved in You, so that they denied Your oneness and worshipped others than You, by empowering them over us, so that they would see that they are upon the truth and we upon falsehood, and You would thereby make us a trial for them. And in the like of what we have said about that the people of interpretation have spoken.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Muḥammad b. ʿAmr told me, he said: Abū ʿĀṣim told us, he said: ʿĪsā told us, and al-Ḥārith told me, he said: al-Ḥasan told us, he said: Warqāʾ told us,
m: both from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid regarding His saying:
make us not a trial for those who disbelieve
. He said: Do not punish us by their hands, nor with a punishment from You, so that they say: Had these been upon the truth, this would not have befallen them

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazīd told us, he said: Saʿīd told us, from Qatāda
m: Our Lord, make us not a trial for those who disbelieve
. He said: He says: Do not make them prevail over us, so that they are put to trial by that; they would see that they prevailed over us only because of a truth they are upon.

c: ʿAlī told me, he said: Abū Ṣāliḥ told us, he said: Muʿāwiya told me, from ʿAlī, from Ibn ʿAbbās
m: make us not a trial for those who disbelieve
. He says: Do not give them power over us so that they put us to trial

x: And His saying:
h
and forgive us, our Lord
and cover our sins for us, by Your pardon of them for us, O our Lord,
h
Indeed, it is You who is the Almighty
He means: the severe in vengeance upon whomever He takes vengeance,
h
the Wise
. He says: the Wise in His management of His creation and His directing them to what is for their good.
And His saying:
h
There has certainly been for you in them an excellent example

. He, exalted be His mention, says: There has certainly been for you, O believers, a good model in those He mentioned—Ibrāhīm and those with him of the prophets, God’s blessings upon them, and the messengers—
h
for whoever hopes in God and the Last Day
. He says: for whoever of you hopes
n
for God’s reward and deliverance on the Last Day.
And His saying:
h
And whoever turns away—then indeed, God is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy

. He, exalted be His mention, says: And whoever turns away from what God commanded him and urged him to, of you or of others, and turns aside from it and withdraws in arrogance, and allies himself with the enemies of God and extends to them affection—then God is the Free of need from his belief in Him, and his obedience to Him, and from all His creation, the Praiseworthy among those who know His favors and bounties to them.
Discussion of the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted:
h
Perhaps God will put, between you and those to whom you were enemies among them, affection. And God is Competent, and God is Forgiving and Merciful (7)

He, exalted be His mention, says: Perhaps God, O believers, will put between you and those you were hostile to among My enemies from the polytheists of Quraysh, affection. And God did that with them, as many of them became Muslim, and became allies and peers
n
to them. And in the like of what we have said about that the people of interpretation have spoken.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Yūnus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said
m: Perhaps God will put, between you and those to whom you were enemies among them, affection
. He said: These polytheists—He has done
it; He has brought them into peace, and put affection between them when Islam came, at the time of the Conquest

x: And His saying:
h
And God is Competent
. He says: And God is able to put affection between you and those among the polytheists to whom you were enemies,
h
and God is Forgiving and Merciful
. He says: And God is forgiving of the sin of one who extended affection to the polytheists, if he repents of it, merciful toward them, that He would punish them
n
after their repentance
n
from it. And in the like of what we have said about that the people of interpretation have spoken.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazīd told us, he said: Saʿīd told us, from Qatāda
m: Perhaps God will put, between you and those to whom you were enemies among them, affection. And God is Competent
and God is Forgiving and Merciful
: He forgives the many sins, merciful to His servants.

x: Discussion of the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted:
h

God does not forbid you from those who do not fight you because of religion and do not expel you from your homes—from being righteous toward them and acting justly toward them. Indeed, God loves those who act justly (8)
He, exalted be His mention, says: God does not forbid you, O believers, from those who did not fight you over religion among the people of Mecca,
h
and did not expel you from your homes—from being righteous toward them and acting justly toward them
. He says: and being fair to them, by your kindness to them and righteousness toward them.

The people of interpretation differed about those meant by this verse; some of them said: By it are meant those who believed in Mecca and did not emigrate, and God permitted the believers to be righteous toward them and kind to them.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Muḥammad b. ʿAmr told us, he said: Abū ʿĀṣim told us, he said: ʿĪsā told us, and al-Ḥārith told me, he said: al-Ḥasan told us, he said: Warqāʾ told us,
m: both from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid regarding His saying:
God does not forbid you from those who do not fight you because of religion
: that you ask forgiveness for them and be righteous toward them and act justly toward them. He said: They are those who believed in Mecca and did not emigrate
. And others said: By it are meant, of those other than the people of Mecca, those who did not emigrate.

x: Mention of those who said that:

c: Muḥammad b. Ibrāhīm al-Anmāṭī told me, he said: Hārūn b. Maʿrūf told us, he said: Bishr b. al-Sarī told us, he said: Muṣʿab b. Thābit told us, from his uncle ʿĀmir b.
m: ʿAbd Allāh b. al-Zubayr, from his father, he said: It was revealed concerning Asmāʾ bint Abī Bakr; she had a mother in the Jāhiliyya called Qutayla
al-ʿUzzā, and she came to her with gifts: lizards

; and she said: I will not accept a gift from you, and you will not enter upon me until the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, permits. ʿĀʾisha mentioned that to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and God revealed:
God does not forbid you from those who do not fight you because of religion
. He said: Ibrāhīm b. al-Ḥajjāj told us, he said:

c: ʿAbd Allāh b. al-Mubārak told us, he said: Muṣʿab b. Thābit told us, from ʿĀmir b.
m: ʿAbd Allāh b. al-Zubayr, from his father, he said: Qutayla daughter of ʿAbd
al-ʿUzzā b. Asʿad of the Banū Mālik b. Ḥisl came to her daughter Asmāʾ bint Abī Bakr. Then he mentioned something similar

. And others said: Rather, by it are meant, of the polytheists of Mecca, those who did not fight the believers and did not expel them from their homes. They said: God abrogated that afterward with the command to fight them.

x: Mention of those who said that:

c: Yūnus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, and I asked him about the saying of God, Mighty and Majestic:

the verse. He said: This has been abrogated; fighting abrogated it; they were commanded to return to them with swords and strive against them with them, striking them, and God set for them a term of four months: either slaughter or Islam

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda
m: the verse. He said: It was abrogated by:
so kill the polytheists wherever you find them

[al-Tawba: 5]. The most correct of the sayings on that is the saying of those who said: By it is meant: God does not forbid you from those who did not fight you over religion, of all kinds of communities and religions, that you be righteous toward them and maintain ties with them and act justly toward them. God, Mighty and Majestic, made general by His saying
those who did not fight you because of religion and did not expel you from your homes

all who have that description, and did not single out some to the exclusion of others. And there is no meaning to the saying of those who said: That is abrogated. For the believer’s kindness to one of the people of war with whom he has a kinship of lineage

, or one with whom he has no kinship nor lineage (1), is neither forbidden nor prohibited, so long as there is in that no pointing out, for him or for the people of war, of a weak point of the people of Islam, or strengthening them with horses or weapons. And the report we mentioned from Ibn al-Zubayr in the story of Asmāʾ and her mother has made clear the soundness of what we said in that.

x: And His saying:
h
Indeed, God loves those who act justly

. He says: Indeed, God loves the equitable, who deal fairly with people and give them the right and justice from themselves, so they are righteous toward those who were righteous toward them, and show kindness to those who showed kindness to them.
Discussion of the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted:
h

God only forbids you from those who fought you because of religion and expelled you from your homes and aided in your expulsion—from taking them as allies. And whoever takes them as allies—those are the wrongdoers (9)
He, exalted be His mention, says: God only forbids you, O believers,
h
from those who fought you because of religion
among the disbelievers of the people of Mecca,
h
and expelled you from your homes and aided in your expulsion—from taking them as allies
. He says: and who helped those who expelled you from your homes in expelling you, from taking them as allies, so that you would be allies and supporters to them,
h
and whoever takes them as allies
. He says: and whoever makes them allies, of you or of others,
h
those are the wrongdoers

. He says: those are the ones who took as allies those whom it is not permissible for them to take as allies, and put their alliance in the wrong place, and opposed the command of God in that. And in the like of what we have said about the meaning of His saying
h
those who fought you because of religion
the people of interpretation have spoken.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Muḥammad b. ʿAmr told me, he said: Abū ʿĀṣim told us, he said: ʿĪsā told us, and al-Ḥārith told me, he said: al-Ḥasan told us, he said: Warqāʾ told us,
m: both from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid:
God only forbids you from those who fought you because of religion
. He said: the disbelievers of the people of Mecca

x: Discussion of the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted:
h

O you who have believed, when the believing women come to you as emigrants, then examine them. God is most knowing of their faith. And if you know them to be believers, then do not return them to the disbelievers; they are not lawful for them, nor are they lawful for them

He, exalted be His mention, says to the believers from among the Companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: O you who have believed, when the believing women come to you as emigrants from the abode of disbelief to the abode of Islam, examine them.
The Messenger of God’s examination of them, when they came as emigrants, was as Abū Kurayb told us, he said:

c: Yūnus b. Bukayr told us, from Qays b.
m: al-Rabīʿ, from al-Agharr b. al-Ṣabbāḥ, from Khalīfa b. Ḥuṣayn, from Abū Naṣr

al-Asadī, he said: Ibn ʿAbbās was asked: How was the Messenger of God’s, may God bless him and grant him peace, examination of the women? He said: He used to examine them: “By God, you did not come out of hatred of a husband; by God, you did not come out of preference for one land over another; by God, you did not come out seeking worldly gain; and by God, you did not come out except from love of God and His Messenger?”

c: Abū Kurayb told us, he said: al-Ḥasan b. ʿAṭiyya told us, from Qays, he said: al-Agharr b. al-Ṣabbāḥ told us, from Khalīfa b.
m: Ḥuṣayn, from Abū Naṣr, from Ibn ʿAbbās regarding:
O you who have believed, when the believing women come to you as emigrants, then examine them
. He said: When a woman came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, he made her swear: “By God, you did not come out.” Then he mentioned something similar

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, that ʿĀʾisha said:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not examine the believing women except by the verse in which God said:
when the believing women come to you pledging allegiance to you that they will not associate anything with God

c: Yūnus b. ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Yūnus told me, from Ibn Shihāb, he said: ʿUrwa b. al-Zubayr told me that
m: ʿĀʾisha, the wife of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When the believing women emigrated to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, [they were examined] by the saying of God:
O Prophet, when the believing women come to you pledging allegiance to you

to the end of the verse. ʿĀʾisha said: Whoever of the believing women affirmed this has affirmed the love; and when they affirmed that by their word, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would say to them: “Go, for I have accepted your pledge.” And no, by God, the hand of the Messenger of God never touched the hand of a woman, but he would take their pledge by speech. ʿĀʾisha said: By God, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, never took [a pledge] from women except as God, Mighty and Majestic, commanded him, and he would say to them when he had taken it from them: “I have accepted your pledge,” in words

c: Muḥammad b. Saʿd told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās
m: O you who have believed, when the believing women come to you as emigrants
: Their examination was that they bear witness that there is no god but God, and that Muḥammad is His servant

c: Muḥammad b. ʿAmr told me, he said: Abū ʿĀṣim told us, he said: ʿĪsā told us, and al-Ḥārith told me, he said: al-Ḥasan told us, he said: Warqāʾ told us,
m: both from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid regarding His saying:
. He said: Ask them what brought them; if what brought them was anger at their husbands, or resentment, or other than that, and they did not believe, then return them to their husbands

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazīd told us, he said: Saʿīd told us, from Qatāda:
m: . He said: Their examination was that they be made to swear by God: What brought you out was not nushūz [rebelliousness], and what brought you out was only love of Islam and its people and eagerness for it? When they said that, it was accepted from them

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda
m: . He said: They swear that they came out only out of desire for Islam and love of God and His Messenger

c: Ibn Ḥumayd told us, he said: Mihrān told us, from Sufyān, from his father,
m: When the believing women come to you (6) as emigrants, then examine them
. He said: It is said: Nothing brought you but love of God and His Messenger, and neither passion for a man among us nor flight from your husband? That is His saying:

c: Yūnus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said:
m: When a woman among the polytheists was angry at her husband and there was a quarrel between him and her, she said: By God, I will emigrate to Muḥammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his Companions. So God, Mighty and Majestic, said:
when the believing women come to you as emigrants, then examine them
: if anger brought her, return her, and if Islam brought her, do not return her

c: Yūnus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: ʿAmr b. al-Ḥārith told me, from Bukayr b.
m: al-Ashajj, he said: Their examination was: Nothing took you out but religion.

x: And His saying:
h
God is most knowing of their faith
. He says: God knows best the faith of whichever women came to you as emigrants.
And His saying:
h
And if you know them to be believers, then do not return them to the disbelievers

. He says: If they acknowledge, at the examination, that by which the contract of faith and entry into Islam is valid for them, then do not, at that point, return them to the disbelievers. It was said to the believers only because a covenant had taken place between the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the polytheists of Quraysh in the truce of al-Ḥudaybiya that the Muslims would return to the polytheists whoever came to them as a Muslim; so that condition was nullified with respect to women when they came as believing emigrants and were examined, and the Muslims found them to be believers, and that was established with them by what we mentioned above, and they were commanded not to return them to the polytheists once it was known that they were believers; and He—majestic be His praise—said to them:
h
If (3) you know them to be believers, then do not return them to the disbelievers; they are not lawful for them, nor are they lawful for them
He says: the believing women are not lawful for the disbelievers, nor are the disbelievers lawful for the believing women. And the reports have come in the like of what we have said about that.
Mention of some of what is reported on that:

c: Ibn Ḥumayd told us, he said: Salama told us, from Muḥammad b.
m: Isḥāq, from al-Zuhrī, he said: I entered upon ʿUrwa b. al-Zubayr while he was writing a letter to Ibn Abī Hunayd
, the companion of al-Walīd b. ʿAbd al-Malik, and he had written to him asking about the saying of God, Mighty and Majestic:
when the believing women come to you as emigrants

. And ʿUrwa b. al-Zubayr wrote to him: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had made a truce with Quraysh in the year of al-Ḥudaybiya on the condition that he return to them whoever came without the permission of his guardian; then, when the women emigrated to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and to Islam, God refused that they be returned to the polytheists if they were examined with the examination of Islam, and they knew that they had come only out of desire for it

x: Discussion of the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted:
h

And give them what they spent. And there is no blame upon you if you marry them when you have given them their dowries. And do not hold to the ties of the disbelieving women, and ask for what you have spent, and let them ask for what they have spent. That is the judgment of God; He judges between you. And God is Knowing, Wise (10)
And His saying:
h
And give them what they spent

. He—majestic be His praise—says: And give the polytheists, whose women came to you as believers—when you knew them to be believers and did not return them to them—what they spent in marrying them, of the dowry. And in the like of what we have said about that the people of interpretation have spoken.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Muḥammad b. Saʿd told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās
m: O you who have believed, when the believing women come to you as emigrants

. He said: Their examination was that they bear witness that there is no god but God, and that Muḥammad is His servant and His Messenger. So when they knew that this was true of them, they did not return them to the disbelievers, and her husband among the disbelievers with whom the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had made a covenant was given the dowry he had given her

c: Muḥammad b. ʿAmr told me, he said: Abū ʿĀṣim told us, he said: ʿĪsā told us, and al-Ḥārith told me, he said: al-Ḥasan told us, he said: Warqāʾ told us,
m: both from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid:
And give them what they spent
: and give their husbands their dowries

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazīd told us, he said: Saʿīd told us, from Qatāda
m: O you who have believed, when the believing women come to you as emigrants, then examine them. God is most knowing of their faith

: This is a ruling that God, Mighty and Majestic, ruled between the people of guidance and the people of misguidance: when women fled from the polytheists—those between whom and the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his Companions there was a covenant—to the Companions of the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they married them, they sent their dowries to their husbands among the polytheists between whom and

the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, there was a covenant; and when women fled from the Companions of the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to the polytheists between whom and the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, there was a covenant, and they married
, they sent their dowries to their husbands among the Companions of the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, he said:
m: It was revealed to him while he was at the lower part of al-Ḥudaybiya; the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had made a truce with them that whoever of them came to him he would return to them; then, when the women came to him, this verse was revealed to him, commanding him to return the dowry to their husbands, and He ruled against the polytheists the like of that, when a woman of the Muslims came to them, that they return the dowry to their husbands. So He said:
and do not hold to the ties of the disbelieving women

c: I was told from al-Ḥusayn,
m: he said: I heard Abū Muʿādh say: ʿUbayd told us, he said: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥāk say regarding His saying:
then examine them. God is most knowing of their faith

: The Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, made covenants with the polytheists and with the People of the Book, so he made a covenant with them and they with him, and in the condition was that they would return the properties and the women; so when one of the wives of the believers escaped him and joined the covenanting party, leaving her religion and choosing polytheism, he returned to her husband what he had spent on her; and when one of the wives of the polytheists joined the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, examined her and asked her: “What brought you out from your people?” If he found that she had come out wanting Islam, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, accepted her and returned to her husband what he had spent on her; and if he found that she had fled from her husband to another with whom she had kinship, while she was clinging to polytheism, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned her to her husband among the polytheists.

c: Yūnus b. ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said
m: O you who have believed, when the believing women come to you as emigrants, then examine them

, the whole verse. He said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, made a truce with the polytheists, among the condition that was stipulated was that you return to us whoever comes to you of us, and we return to you whoever comes to us of you; so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever comes to us from you, we will return him to you, and whoever comes to you from us and chooses disbelief over faith, we have no need of them.” He said: But God refused that for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the case of women, and did not refuse it in the case of men; so God, Mighty and Majestic, said:
when the believing women come to you as emigrants, then examine them
and give them what they spent

c: Yūnus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: ʿAmr b. al-Ḥārith told me, from Bukayr b.
m: al-Ashajj, he said: Between the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the polytheists there was a truce regarding whichever women fled; so when a polytheist woman fled, the Muslims gave her husband his expenditure on her, and the Muslims would do so; and if neither these nor those gave, the Muslims paid out, for the Muslim whose wife had gone away, her expenditure.

x: And His saying:
h
And there is no blame upon you if you marry them when you have given them their dowries

. He, exalted be His mention, says: And there is no blame upon you, O believers, in marrying these women emigrants who joined you from the abode of war, separated from their husbands, even if they have husbands in the abode of war, when you know them to be believers, when you have given them their dowries (ujūr). By ujūr He means: the ṣaduqāt [dowries]. Qatāda used to say: When women fled from the polytheists—those between whom and the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his Companions there was a covenant—to the Companions of the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they married them, they sent their dowries to their husbands among the polytheists between whom and the Companions of the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, there was a covenant.

c: Bishr told us that, he said: Yazīd told us, he said: Saʿīd told us,
m: . And al-Zuhrī used to say: God commanded the return of their dowries to them only if they were detained from them, only if they returned to the Muslims the dowry of those of their women whom they detained from them.

c: Ibn Ḥumayd told us that, he said: Salama told us, from Ibn Isḥāq,
Yūnus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said
m: And there is no blame upon you if you marry them
: even though she has a husband there; because Islam separated them, once their wombs have been cleared

x: And His saying:
h
And do not hold to the ties of the disbelieving women

. He—majestic be His praise—says to the believers in Him from among the Companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: Do not hold, O believers, to the ropes of the disbelieving women and their bonds. Al-kawāfir is the plural of kāfira, and al-ʿiṣam is the plural of ʿiṣma, which is that by which one holds fast, of contract and bond; and this is a prohibition from God to the believers against proceeding
n
to marry polytheist women of the idol-worshippers, and a command to them to separate from them. And in the like of what we have said about that the people of interpretation have spoken.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Yaʿqūb b. Ibrāhīm told me, he said: Yaḥyā b. Saʿīd al-Qaṭṭān told us, he said: ʿAbd Allāh b. al-Mubārak told us, he said: Maʿmar told us, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUrwa, from al-Miswar b.
m: Makhrama and Marwān b. al-Ḥakam, that some believing women came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, after he had written the document of the settlement between him and Quraysh; so God revealed:
O you who have believed, when the believing women come to you as emigrants
the ties of the disbelieving women
. So ʿUmar divorced that day two wives he had in polytheism; Muʿāwiya b. Abī Sufyān married one of them, and Ṣafwān b. Umayya the other

c: Yūnus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Yūnus told me, from Ibn Shihāb, he said:
m: It has reached us that the verse of examination, in which the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, protracted (mādda)

[the term] with the disbelievers of Quraysh, was on account of the covenant that was between the disbelievers of Quraysh and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace; so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to return to the disbelievers of Quraysh what they had spent on their women who became Muslim and emigrated—while their husbands were disbelievers—because of the covenant that was between the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and them; and had they been people at war with whom there was between them and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, no term and contract, he would not have returned anything to them of what they had spent; and God ruled for the believers against the people of the term among the disbelievers the like of that. God said:
O you who have believed, when the believing women come to you as emigrants, then examine them

. So the believers divorced, when this verse was revealed, every disbelieving woman who was married to one of them; ʿUmar b. al-Khaṭṭāb, may God be pleased with him, divorced his wife, the daughter of Abū Umayya b. al-Mughīra of the Banū Makhzūm, and Muʿāwiya b. Abī Sufyān married her; and the daughter of Jarwal of Khuzāʿa, and Abū Jahm b. Ḥudhāfa al-ʿAdawī married her; and God made that a ruling by which He ruled between the believers and the polytheists in this term that was

c: Ibn Ḥumayd told us, he said: Salama told us, from Muḥammad b.
m: Isḥāq, he said: And al-Zuhrī said: When this verse was revealed:
O you who have believed, when the believing women come to you
and do not hold to the ties of the disbelieving women

, among those whom ʿUmar b. al-Khaṭṭāb, may God be pleased with him, divorced was his wife Qurayba daughter of Abū Umayya b. al-Mughīra, and Muʿāwiya b. Abī Sufyān married her after him, both being in their polytheism in Mecca; and Umm Kulthūm daughter of Jarwal al-Khuzāʿiyya, the mother of ʿUbayd
Allāh b. ʿUmar, and Abū Jahm b. Ḥudhāfa

b. Ghānim, a man of his people, married her, both being in their polytheism; and Ṭalḥa b. ʿUbayd Allāh b. ʿUthmān b. ʿAmr al-Taymī: he had Arwā daughter of Rabīʿa b. al-Ḥārith b. ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, and Islam separated them when the Qurʾān forbade holding to the ties of the disbelieving women; Ṭalḥa had emigrated while she was in Mecca upon the religion of her people; then after Ṭalḥa, in Islam, [Khālid b.]

Saʿīd b. al-ʿĀṣ b. Umayya b. ʿAbd Shams married her; and among those who fled to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, of the wives of the disbelievers, of those between whom and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, there was no covenant, was—so he detained her and married her to a man of the Muslims—Umayma bint Bishr al-Anṣāriyya, one of the women of the Banū Umayya b. Zayd of

Aws Allāh; she had been with Thābit b. al-Daḥdāḥa, and she fled from him—he being at that time a disbeliever—to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, married her to Sahl b. Ḥunayf, one of the Banū ʿAmr b. ʿAwf, and she bore ʿAbd Allāh b. Sahl

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told me, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī:
m: and do not hold to the ties of the disbelieving women
. Al-Zuhrī said: So ʿUmar divorced two wives he had in Mecca

c: Muḥammad b. ʿAmr told me, he said: Abū ʿĀṣim told us, he said: ʿĪsā told us, and al-Ḥārith told me, he said: al-Ḥasan told us, he said: Warqāʾ told us,
m: both from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid:
and do not hold to the ties of the disbelieving women
. He said: The Companions of Muḥammad were commanded to divorce their wives who were disbelievers in Mecca, who had stayed with the disbelievers

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazīd told us, he said: Saʿīd told us, from Qatāda
m: and do not hold to the ties of the disbelieving women
: the polytheist women of the Arabs who refused Islam; he was commanded to let them go.

c: Yūnus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said
m: and do not hold to the ties of the disbelieving women
: When a woman disbelieves, do not hold her; release her; separation occurred between her and her husband when she disbelieved. The reciters differed in the reading of His saying:
and do not hold to the ties of the disbelieving women
; most of the reciters of the Ḥijāz, Medina, Kufa and Syria read
. And Abū ʿAmr read (tumassikū) with tashdīd
, and it is mentioned that it is the reading of al-Ḥasan
. Those who read it lightened took as a proof:
then retention in a recognized manner
[al-Baqara: 229]. The correct view on that is that they are two well-known readings and two famous dialects, reported from the Arabs: amsaktu bihi, and masaktu, and tamassaktu bihi.

evidence.text: The reciters differed in the reading of His saying: {and do not hold to the ties of the disbelieving women}; most of the reciters of the Ḥijāz, Medina, Kufa and Syria read {wa-lā tumsikū} with the sīn lightened (1).
And Abū ʿAmr read (tumassikū) with tashdīd (2), and it is mentioned that it is the reading of al-Ḥasan (3).

x: And His saying:
h
and ask for what you have spent, and let them ask for what they have spent

. He, exalted be His mention, says to the husbands of those women who, of the believers, joined the polytheists in Mecca from the abode of Islam, of the disbelievers of Quraysh: And ask, O believers, whose wives went away and joined the polytheists, what you spent on your wives who joined them, of the dowry, from whoever married them among them; and let the polytheists among them whose wives joined you as believers ask you, when they have married among you, from whoever married her among you, what they spent on them of the dowry. And in the like of what we have said about that the people of interpretation have spoken.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Yūnus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Yūnus told me, from Ibn Shihāb, he said:
m: The believers acknowledged the ruling of God and paid what they were commanded of the expenditures of the polytheists that they had spent on their wives, while the polytheists refused to acknowledge God’s ruling in what was imposed upon them of paying the expenditures of the Muslims

c: Muḥammad b. ʿAmr told me, he said: Abū ʿĀṣim told us, he said: ʿĪsā told us, and al-Ḥārith told me, he said: al-Ḥasan told us, he said: Warqāʾ told us,
m: both from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid regarding the saying of God:
and ask for what you have spent, and let them ask for what they have spent

. He said: Whatever went away of the wives of the Companions of Muḥammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, to the disbelievers, let the disbelievers give them [the husbands] their dowries and keep them; and whatever went away of the wives of the disbelievers to the Companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, is the like of that, in a truce that was between Muḥammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Quraysh

x: And His saying:
h
That is the judgment of God; He judges between you

. He, exalted be His mention, says: This ruling that I have ruled between you in your affair, O believers, namely that the polytheists be asked for what you spent on your wives who joined them, and that they be commanded to ask you the like of that regarding their wives who joined you, is the judgment of God, who judges between you; so do not transgress it, for it is the truth, other than which nothing is to be heard. So the believers among the Companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, as is mentioned, submitted to the command of God and His judgment, while the polytheists refused it and demanded fulfilment of the conditions they had stipulated among themselves in that truce. And the reports and narratives came to that effect from the people of the Sīra and others.
Mention of the narration on that:

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, he said:
m: As for the believers, they acknowledged the ruling of God, and as for the polytheists, they refused to acknowledge; so God, Mighty and Majestic, revealed:
And if anything of your wives escapes you to the disbelievers

c: Ibn Ḥumayd told us, he said: Salama told us, from Ibn Isḥāq, from al-Zuhrī, he said:
m: That is the judgment of God; He judges between you

; so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, kept the women and returned the men, and asked what God commanded him to ask of the dowries of the women whom they detained of them, and that they return to them the like of what they would return to them if they did so; and had it not been for this ruling that God ruled, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would have returned the women as he returned the men; and had it not been for the truce and covenant between him and Quraysh on the day of al-Ḥudaybiya, he would have kept the women and not returned any dowry to them; and likewise he would do with whoever came to him of Muslim women before the covenant

x: And His saying:
h
and God is Knowing, Wise
. He—majestic be His praise—says: God is possessed of knowledge of what sets His creation right, and other matters, wise in His management of them.
Discussion of the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted:
h
And if any of your wives escapes you to the disbelievers and you have a turn, then give those whose wives have gone the like of what they spent. And fear God, in whom you are believers (11)

He—majestic be His praise—says to the believers from among the Companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: And if anything of your wives escapes you, O believers, to the disbelievers, and joins them.
The people of interpretation differed regarding the disbelievers meant by His saying:
h
to the disbelievers
; who are they?

Some of them said: They are the disbelievers between whom and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, there was no covenant. They said: And the meaning of the speech is: and if anything of your wives escapes you to those of the disbelievers with whom you have no covenant.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Muḥammad b. ʿAmr told me, he said: Abū ʿĀṣim told us, he said: ʿĪsā told us, and al-Ḥārith told me, he said: al-Ḥasan told us, he said: Warqāʾ told us,
m: both from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid regarding His saying:
And if anything of your wives escapes you to the disbelievers
: those between whom and you there is no covenant

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazīd told us, he said: Saʿīd told us, from Qatāda:
m: And if anything of your wives escapes you to the disbelievers

: when they fled from the Companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to disbelievers between whom and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, there was no covenant

c: Ibn Ḥumayd told us, he said: Mihrān told us, from Sufyān, from Ḥabīb b.
m: And if anything of your wives escapes you to the disbelievers
with whom there is no covenant. And others said: Rather, they are the disbelievers of Quraysh who were people of truce, and that is the saying of al-Zuhrī.

c: Yūnus told me
m: of that, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Yūnus told me from him

x: And His saying:
h
and you have a turn
The reciters differed in the reading of that; most of the reciters of the cities read it
h
fa-ʿāqabtum

with an alif, on the pattern of “fāʿaltum,” meaning: you obtained from them a ʿuqbā [a turn, a recompense]. And Ḥumayd al-Aʿraj read it, as is reported from him: (fa-ʿaqqabtum), on the pattern of “faʿʿaltum,” with shadda on the qāf
n
. And in the difference of wording the two are like His saying:
h
and do not turn your cheek away from people
[Luqmān: 18], and (tuṣāʿir), with the closeness of their meanings
n

h
fa-ʿāqabtum
