And Ḥumayd al-Aʿraj read it, as is reported from him: (fa-ʿaqqabtum), on the pattern of “faʿʿaltum,” with shadda on the qāf (5).
Abū Jaʿfar said: The better of the two readings in my view is the reading of those who read it {fa-ʿāqabtum} with an alif, because of the consensus of the authoritative body of reciters upon it.

x: And His saying:
h
then give those whose wives have gone the like of what they spent
. He says: So give those of you whose wives went away to the disbelievers the like of what they spent on them of the dowry.
The people of interpretation differed about the property from which the one whose wife went away to the polytheists was commanded to be given; some of them said: They were commanded to give them from
n
the dowry of those women of the polytheists who joined them.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Yūnus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Yūnus told me, from al-Zuhrī, he said:
m: The believers acknowledged the ruling of God and paid what they were commanded of the expenditures of the polytheists that they had spent on their wives, while the polytheists refused to acknowledge the ruling of God in what He imposed upon them of paying the expenditures of the Muslims; so God said to the believers:
And if any of your wives escapes you to the disbelievers and you have a turn, then give those whose wives have gone the like of what they spent. And fear God, in whom you are believers

. So had a woman of the wives of the believers gone away to the polytheists after this verse, the believers would return to her husband the expenditure he had spent on her out of the ʿuqb that was in their hands, which they had been commanded to return to the polytheists of their expenditures that they had spent on their wives who believed and emigrated; then they would return to the polytheists any surplus that remained for them. And the ʿuqb is what was in the hands of the believers of the dowry of the women of the disbelievers when they believed and emigrated

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, he said:
m: And if any of your wives escapes you to the disbelievers and you have a turn, then give those whose wives have gone the like of what they spent

. So God commanded the believers to return the dowry when a woman of the Muslims went away who had a husband, that the Muslims return to him the dowry of his wife, from a dowry, if it was in their hands, of what they were commanded to return to the polytheists
. And others said: Rather, they were commanded to give him from the spoil or the fayʾ.

x: Mention of those who said that:

c: Muḥammad b. Saʿd told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās
m: And if any of your wives escapes you to the disbelievers and you have a turn, then give those whose wives have gone the like of what they spent. And fear God, in whom you are believers

. He means: if the wife of a man of the Emigrants joined the disbelievers, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, commanded that he be given from the spoil the like of what he had spent

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid,
m: that they were commanded to return to them from the spoil. And Mujāhid used to read:

c: Muḥammad b. ʿAmr told me, he said: Abū ʿĀṣim told us, he said: ʿĪsā told us, and al-Ḥārith told me, he said: al-Ḥasan told us, he said: Warqāʾ told us,
m: both from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid:
. He says: you obtained booty from Quraysh or others,
then give those whose wives have gone the like of what they spent

c: Ibn Ḥumayd told us, he said: Mihrān told us, from Sufyān, from Ḥabīb b.
m: And if any of your wives escapes you to the disbelievers
. He said: Those with whom there is no covenant between them and them
went away to the polytheists; then there is paid to her husband the dowry of the like of her;
then give those whose wives have gone the like of what they spent. And fear God
. He said: The dowry of the like of her is paid to her husband

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazīd told us, he said: Saʿīd told us, from Qatāda
m: And if any of your wives escapes you to the disbelievers and you have a turn, then give those whose wives have gone the like of what they spent. And fear God

: When they fled from the Companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to disbelievers between whom and the Prophet of God there was no covenant, and the Companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, obtained booty, her husband was given what he had given her, out of all the booty; then they would divide their booty

c: Aḥmad b. Yūsuf told me, he said: al-Qāsim told us, he said:
m: I heard al-Kisāʾī report, from Zāʾida, from al-Aʿmash, from Muslim, from Masrūq, that he read it
. And he explained it: so you took spoil

c: Aḥmad told us, he said: al-Qāsim told us, he said: Hushaym told us, from Mughīra, from Ibrāhīm
Ibn Ḥumayd told us, he said: Salama told us, from Ibn Isḥāq, he said:
m: We asked al-Zuhrī about this verse and the saying of God in it:
And if any of your wives escapes you to the disbelievers

the verse. He said: He says: If someone of you loses his wife to the disbelievers, and no woman comes to you for whom you take the like of what they take from you, then compensate him from fayʾ if you obtain it

c: And others said regarding that what Yūnus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said
m: And if any of your wives escapes you to the disbelievers and you have a turn

. He said: A woman of the people of Islam went out to the polytheists, and no one else went out. He said: Then a woman of the polytheists came, and the people said: This is your ʿuqba [turn]; she has come to you. So God said:
And if any of your wives escapes you to the disbelievers and you have a turn
: you held back the one who came to you of them on account of what is owed to you with them,
then give those whose wives have gone the like of what they spent

c: Then God informed them that
m: there is no blame upon them, if they did what they did, in marrying them once her womb has been cleared. He said: So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, summoned [the one] whose wife had gone away to the disbelievers, and said to this woman who had come from the polytheists: “Is this the husband of the one who went away—shall I marry you to him?” She said: O Messenger of God, God has excused the wife of this man for fleeing from him; no, by God, I have no need of him. Then he called al-Bakhtarī, a stout man, and said: “This one?” She said: Yes. And she was among those who came from Mecca. And the most correct of the sayings on that in my view is to say: God, Mighty and Majestic, commanded the believers in this verse to give the one whose wife fled from among the believers to the people of disbelief—when they have a ʿuqbā against the people of disbelief, either through booty they obtain from them, or through the joining of some of their women to them—the like of what they spent on the one who fled to them from among them; and He did not specify giving them that from one property to the exclusion of another; so they must give them that from all the properties we have mentioned.

evidence.text: Aḥmad b. Yūsuf told me, he said: al-Qāsim told us, he said: I heard al-Kisāʾī report, from Zāʾida, from al-Aʿmash, from Muslim, from Masrūq, that he read it {fa-ʿāqabtum}.

x: And His saying:
h
And fear God, in whom you are believers
He says: And fear God, whom you affirm, O believers; so fear Him by performing His obligations and avoiding disobedience to Him.
Discussion of the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted:
h

O Prophet, when the believing women come to you pledging allegiance to you that they will not associate anything with God, nor steal, nor commit unlawful sexual intercourse, nor kill their children, nor bring forth a slander they invent between their hands and their feet, nor disobey you in what is right, then accept their pledge and ask forgiveness for them from God. Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful (12)
He, exalted be His mention, says to His Prophet Muḥammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: O Prophet, when the women who believe in God come to you,
h

pledging allegiance to you that they will not associate anything with God, nor steal, nor commit unlawful sexual intercourse, nor kill their children, nor bring forth a slander they invent between their hands and their feet

. He says: nor bring a lie that they fabricate concerning a newborn found between their hands and their feet. And the meaning of the speech is only: nor attach to their husbands those who are not their children. And in the like of what we have said about that the people of interpretation have spoken.
Mention of those who said that:

c: ʿAlī told me, he said: Abū Ṣāliḥ told us, he said: Muʿāwiya told me, from ʿAlī, from Ibn ʿAbbās
m: nor bring forth a slander they invent between their hands and their feet
. He says: they do not attach to their husbands those who are not their children

x: And His saying:
h
nor disobey you in what is right

. He says: nor disobey you, O Muḥammad, in what is right of the command of God, Mighty and Majestic, with which you command them. And it is mentioned that that right thing in which they were stipulated not to disobey the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is wailing (al-niyāḥa).
Mention of those who said that:

c: ʿAlī told us, he said: Abū Ṣāliḥ told us, he said: Muʿāwiya told us, from ʿAlī, from Ibn ʿAbbās
m: nor disobey you in what is right
. He says: they shall not wail

c: Ibn Bashshār told us, he said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān told us, he said: ʿAbd Allāh b. al-Mubārak told us, from Sufyān, from Manṣūr, from Sālim b.
m: nor disobey you in what is right

c: Ibn Bashshār told us, he said: Abū Aḥmad told us, he said: Sufyān told us, from Manṣūr, from Sālim b.
m: Abī al-Jaʿd, the like of it.

c: Ibn Ḥumayd told us, he said: Jarīr told us, from Manṣūr, from Sālim,
Muḥammad b. ʿUbayd al-Muḥāribī told us, he said: Mūsā b. ʿUmayr told us, from Abū Ṣāliḥ
m: nor disobey you in what is right

c: Ibn Ḥumayd told us, he said: Mihrān told us, from Sufyān, from Manṣūr, from Sālim b.
m: nor disobey you in what is right
. He said: wailing. He said: Mihrān told us, from Sufyān, from Zayd b. Aslam:
nor disobey you in what is right
. He said: They shall not scratch a face, nor tear a garment-opening, nor call out for woe, nor recite poetry

c: Muḥammad b. Saʿd told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said:
m: The examination of the women was that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, commanded ʿUmar b. al-Khaṭṭāb, may God be pleased with him, and said: “Say to them: The Messenger of God pledges you on the condition that you do not associate anything with God.” And Hind bint ʿUtba b. Rabīʿa—who had split open the belly of Ḥamza, God’s mercy upon him—was disguised among the women, and she said: If I speak he will recognize me, and if he recognizes me he will kill me. She had disguised herself only out of fear of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace; and the women who were with Hind fell silent and refused to speak. Hind said, while disguised: How can he accept from women what he did not accept from men? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, looked at her and said to ʿUmar: “Say to them: nor steal.” Hind said: By God, I take from Abū Sufyān small things, and I do not know whether they are lawful for me or not. Abū Sufyān said: Whatever you have taken, whether past or remaining, is lawful for you. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, laughed and recognized her, and called her, and she came to him, took his hand and sought refuge with him, and he said: “You are Hind?” She said: May God pardon what is past. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, turned away from her, and said: “
.” She said: O Messenger of God, does a free woman commit unlawful intercourse? He said: “No, by God, a free woman does not commit unlawful intercourse.” He said: “
.” Hind said: You killed them on the day of Badr, so you and they know best. He said: “
nor bring forth a slander they invent between their hands and their feet, nor disobey you in what is right
.” He said: He forbade them to wail; and the people of the Jāhiliyya used to tear garments, scratch faces, cut hair, and call out for destruction and woe

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazīd told us, he said: Saʿīd told us, from Qatāda:
m: O Prophet, when the believing women come to you pledging allegiance to you

: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took from them on that day [the pledge against] wailing, and: “Do not speak with men, except a man of you who is a maḥram.” Then ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. ʿAwf said: O Prophet of God, we have guests, and we are away from our women. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Those are not whom I meant; those are not whom I meant”

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda:
m: nor disobey you in what is right

. He said: It is wailing; they were bound not to wail, and not to be alone in conversation with men except with a maḥram. He said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. ʿAwf said: We are away and we have guests. He said: “Those are not whom I meant”

c: Ibn Bashshār told us, he said: Sulaymān told us, he said: Abū Hilāl told us, he said: Qatāda told us
m: nor disobey you in what is right
. He said: they shall not speak to a man.

c: Yūnus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn ʿAyyāsh told me, from Sulaymān b.
m: , from ʿAmr b. Shuʿayb, from his father, from his grandfather, he said: Umayma bint Ruqayqa came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to pledge to him on Islam, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to her: “I pledge you on the condition that you do not associate anything with God, nor steal, nor commit unlawful intercourse, nor kill your child, nor bring a slander that you fabricate between your hands and your feet, nor wail, nor display yourself with the display of the former Jāhiliyya”

c: Ibn Ḥumayd told us, he said: Mihrān told us, from Sufyān, from Muḥammad b.
m: al-Munkadir, from Umayma bint Ruqayqa, she said: Some women came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to pledge to him, and he said: “In what you are able and can bear.” We said: God and His Messenger are more merciful to us than we are to ourselves

c: Muḥammad b. ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿAbd al-Ḥakam told us, he said: My father and Shuʿayb b. al-Layth told us, from al-Layth, he said: Khālid b. Yazīd told us, from Ibn Abī Hilāl, from Ibn al-Munkadir, that Umayma informed him that
m: she entered upon the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with some women, and they said: O Messenger of God, extend your hand that we may shake hands with you. He said: “I do not shake hands with women, but I will take [the pledge] from you.” So he took it from us until he reached: “
nor disobey you in what is right
.” He said: “In what you are able and can bear.” They said: God and His Messenger are more merciful to us than we are to ourselves

c: Ibn Ḥumayd told us, he said: Hārūn told us, from ʿAmr, from ʿĀṣim, from Ibn Sīrīn, from Umm ʿAṭiyya al-Anṣāriyya, she said:
m: Among the right things he stipulated upon us when we pledged was that we not wail. A woman [of the Banū so-and-so]
said: The Banū so-and-so assisted me
[in wailing], so not until I repay them. She went off and assisted them, then came and pledged. He said: None of them fulfilled it except her and Umm Sulaym bint Milḥān, the mother of Anas b. Mālik

c: Abū Kurayb told us, he said: Abū Nuʿaym told us, he said:
m: told us, he said: Muṣʿab b. Nūḥ al-Anṣārī told us, he said: I met an old woman of ours who was among those who pledged to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace; she said: I came to him to pledge to him, and he took from us, among what he took: “and do not wail.” An old woman said: O Prophet of God, some people had assisted me in misfortunes that befell me, and a misfortune has befallen them, and I want to assist them. He said: “Go and repay them.” Then she came and pledged to him. He said: That is the right thing of which God said:
nor disobey you in what is right

c: Abū Kurayb told us, he said: Wakīʿ told us, from Yazīd,
m: the client of al-Ṣahbāʾ, from Shahr b. Ḥawshab, from Umm Salama, from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding His saying:
nor disobey you in what is right

c: Abū Kurayb told us, he said: Yūnus told us, he said: Muḥammad b. Isḥāq told us, from Muḥammad b.
m: al-Munkadir, from Umayma bint Ruqayqa al-Taymiyya, she said: I pledged to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, among some Muslim women, and we said to him: We have come to you, O Messenger of God, to pledge to you that we shall not associate anything with God, nor steal, nor commit unlawful intercourse, nor kill our children, nor bring a slander that we fabricate between our hands and our feet, nor disobey you in what is right. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “In what you are able and can bear.” We said: God and His Messenger are more merciful to us than we are to ourselves; and we said: Take our pledge, O Messenger of God. He said: “Go, for I have accepted your pledge; my saying to a hundred women is like my saying to one woman.” And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not shake hands with any of us

c: Abū Kurayb told us, he said: Yūnus b. Bukayr told us, from ʿĪsā b.
m: ʿAbd Allāh al-Tamīmī, from Muḥammad b. al-Munkadir, from Umayma [bint Ruqayqa]

, the maternal aunt of Fāṭima, the daughter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: I heard her say: We pledged to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he took from us that we not associate anything with God. Then he mentioned the like of the ḥadīth of Muḥammad b. Isḥāq. Muḥammad b. Bashshār told us, he said:

c: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān told us, he said: Sufyān told us, from Muḥammad b.
m: al-Munkadir, from Umayma bint Ruqayqa, she said: I came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, among some women, pledging to him; she said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, took from us what is in the Qurʾān:
that they will not associate anything with God

the verse. Then he said: “In what you are able and can bear.” We said: O Messenger of God, will you not shake hands with us? He said: “I do not shake hands with women; my saying to one woman is only like my saying to a hundred women”

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥīm al-Barqī told us, he said: ʿAmr b. Abī Salama told us, from Zuhayr, from Mūsā b.
m: ʿUqba, from Muḥammad b. al-Munkadir, from Umayma bint Ruqayqa, from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, similarly

c: I was told from al-Ḥusayn,
m: he said: I heard Abū Muʿādh say: ʿUbayd told us, he said: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥāk say regarding His saying:
nor disobey you in what is right
: And the right is what was stipulated upon them in the pledge: that they follow his command.

c: Yūnus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said
m: nor disobey you in what is right

. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is His Prophet and His chosen one among His creation, yet He did not make lawful for him the matters of any command except by a condition; He did not say:
and leave it, until He said:

. So how should anyone be obeyed in other than what is right, when God has stipulated this upon His Prophet? He said: So the right is every right thing that he commanded them in all matters, and it is fitting for them not to disobey

c: Muḥammad b. Sinān al-Qazzāz told us, [Isḥāq b. Idrīs told us,
m: , he said: Ismāʿīl b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. ʿAṭiyya told me, from his grandmother Umm ʿAṭiyya, she said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to Medina, he gathered the women of the Anṣār in a house, then sent ʿUmar b. al-Khaṭṭāb to us, and he stood at the door and greeted us, and they returned [the greeting], or: we returned it to him, then he said: I am the messenger of the Messenger of God to you. She said: We said: Welcome to the Messenger of God, and to the messenger of the Messenger of God. He said: Do you pledge not to associate anything with God, nor steal, nor commit unlawful intercourse? She said: We said: Yes. She said: So he stretched out his hand from outside the door or the house, and we stretched out our hands from inside the house, then he said: O God, bear witness. She said: And he commanded us, regarding the two festivals, to bring out the menstruating women and the young unmarried women, and that Friday prayer is not obligatory upon us, and he forbade us to follow the funeral procession. Ismāʿīl said: I asked my grandmother about the saying of God:
nor disobey you in what is right

c: Muḥammad b. ʿAbd al-Raḥīm al-Barqī told me, he said: ʿAmr b. Abī Salama told us, from Zuhayr
m: nor disobey you in what is right
. He said: A man shall not be alone with a woman.

x: And His saying:
h
then accept their pledge
. He—majestic be His praise—says: When the believing women come to you pledging allegiance to you on these conditions, then accept their pledge,
h
and ask forgiveness for them from God
. He says: ask God for them that He overlook their sins and cover them for them, by His pardon of them.
h
Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful
. He says: Indeed, God is a coverer of the sins of whoever repents to Him of his sins, so that He does not punish him for them after his repentance from them.
Discussion of the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted:
h
O you who have believed, do not take as allies a people with whom God is angry. They have despaired of the Hereafter just as the disbelievers have despaired of the companions of the graves (13)
He, exalted be His mention, says to the believers in Him from among the Companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace:
h
O you who have believed, do not take as allies a people with whom God is angry
, of the Jews,
h
They have despaired of the Hereafter just as the disbelievers have despaired of the companions of the graves
The people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of His saying:
h
They have despaired of the Hereafter just as the disbelievers have despaired of the companions of the graves
; some of them said: The meaning of that: These people with whom God is angry, of the Jews, have despaired of God’s reward for them
n
in the Hereafter, and of being resurrected, just as the living disbelievers have despaired of their dead who are in the graves, that they will return to them.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Muḥammad b. Saʿd told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās
m: O you who have believed, do not take as allies a people with whom God is angry
the verse. He means: whoever of those who disbelieved has died, the living among those who disbelieved have despaired that they will return to them, or that God will resurrect them

c: Ibn al-Muthannā told us, he said: Muḥammad b. Jaʿfar told us, he said: Shuʿba told us, from Manṣūr b.
m: , that he said regarding this verse:
They have despaired of the Hereafter just as the disbelievers have despaired of the companions of the graves
. He said: The living disbelievers have despaired of the dead

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda
m: They have despaired of the Hereafter
. He says: they have despaired of being resurrected, just as the disbelievers have despaired that the companions of the graves who died will return to them

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazīd told us, he said: Saʿīd told us, from Qatāda
m: O you who have believed, do not take as allies a people with whom God is angry. They have despaired of the Hereafter
the verse: The disbeliever does not hope to meet his dead, nor his reward

c: I was told from al-Ḥusayn,
m: he said: I heard Abū Muʿādh say: ʿUbayd told us, he said: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥāk say regarding His saying:
They have despaired of the Hereafter just as the disbelievers have despaired of the companions of the graves

. He says: whoever of those who disbelieved has died, the living among them have despaired that they will return to them, or that God will resurrect them (2). And others said: Rather, the meaning of that: They have despaired of the Hereafter, that God will have mercy on them in it or forgive them, just as the disbelievers who are companions of graves—who have died and gone to the graves—have despaired of God’s mercy and His pardon of them in the Hereafter; for they have become certain of God’s punishment of them.

x: Mention of those who said that:

c: Ibn al-Muthannā told us, he said: Muḥammad b. Jaʿfar told us, from Shuʿba, from al-Ḥakam, from Mujāhid
m: They have despaired of the Hereafter just as the disbelievers have despaired of the companions of the graves
. He said: The companions of the graves, those who are in the graves, have despaired of the Hereafter.

c: Muḥammad b. ʿAmr told me, he said: Abū ʿĀṣim told us, he said:
m: told us, and al-Ḥārith told me, he said: al-Ḥasan told us, he said: Warqāʾ told us, both from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid regarding His saying:
They have despaired of the Hereafter just as the disbelievers have despaired of the companions of the graves
. He said: of the reward of the Hereafter, when their deeds became clear to them and they beheld the Fire

c: Ibn al-Muthannā told us, he said: Muḥammad told us, he said: Shuʿba told us, from Simāk, from ʿIkrima, that he said
m: They have despaired of the Hereafter
the verse. He said: The companions of the graves have despaired of the Hereafter

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, he said: al-Kalbī said:
m: They have despaired of the Hereafter

. He means: the Jews and the Christians; he says: they have despaired of the reward of the Hereafter and its honor, just as the disbelievers who have died—so they are in the graves—have despaired of Paradise, when they saw their seat in the Fire

c: Yūnus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said
m: do not take as allies a people

the verse. He said: These disbelievers have despaired of having a Hereafter, just as the disbelievers who died, who are in the graves, have despaired of having a Hereafter; because of what they saw of the matter of the Hereafter; so just as those

disbelievers despaired, so too these disbelievers have despaired. He said: And the people with whom God is angry are the Jews; they are the ones who have despaired of having a Hereafter, just as the disbelievers before them, from among the companions of the graves, despaired; because they knew the Book of God, and persisted in disbelief in it. And what did they do, when they knew

c: Ibn Ḥumayd told us, he said: Jarīr told us, from Manṣūr
m: They have despaired of the Hereafter

the verse. He said: They have despaired of having the reward of the Hereafter, just as those who are in the graves of the disbelievers have despaired of any good, when they beheld the punishment and the humiliation (2). And the better of the two sayings on that in my view is the saying of those who said: These people with whom God is angry, of the Jews, have despaired of God’s reward for them in the Hereafter and His honoring of them, because of their disbelief and their denial of His Messenger Muḥammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, despite their knowledge that he is a prophet of God, just as the disbelievers among them who passed before them and perished, and became companions of the graves, despaired—being upon the like of what these are upon, of denying ʿĪsā, God’s blessings upon him, and other messengers—of God’s reward and His honoring them. And we said that this is the better of the two sayings regarding the interpretation of the verse because the dead, believers and disbelievers alike, have despaired of returning to the world, or of being resurrected before the coming of the Hour; so there is no ground for specifying the report about the disbelievers with that, when the believers share with them in despair of that. End of the commentary on Sūrat al-Mumtaḥana.

Ḍibāb is the plural of ḍabb, the well-known animal; as for ṣanāb, it is a condiment made from mustard and raisins. See Lisān al-ʿArab (ḍ-b-b, ṣ-n-b).

notes.en: In Ṣ, T1, T2 and T3: “qarṭ.” Al-aqiṭ is something made from skimmed buttermilk, which is cooked and then left until it forms whey. Lisān al-ʿArab (ʾ-q-ṭ).
